I've never read a Marvel comic in my life, where do I start?

I usually suggest starting at the original Civil War for a number of reasons. The Secret Wars version won't exactly be a reboot, but going from one to the other could get you burnt out. Are you interested in reading the other Secret Wars titles? If so, it's going to depend how far into it you're going to get.

Secret Wars has built from everything Hickman has written since Dark Reign: Fantastic Four: The Bridge in 2009. After that, he goes into Fantastic Four and FF (I've got a post I'm filling in with some important plot points and prophecies they give there to see what's still relevant). That's about thirty or forty issues. Immediately following that, he writes Avengers and New Avengers.

Matt Fraction's Invincible Iron Man was pretty great. Volumes 2 through 5 are a decently self-contained story, which also takes place during Dark Reign (the time period where the Super Human Registration Act is still in effect and Norman Osborn runs SHIELD).

Do not read Avengers vs X-Men first. It comes at the end of a decade of X-Men being on the brink of extinction and being bullied by the government, and you'll have to be on Wikipedia reading up on the Phoenix Force a fair deal. That epic story starts with House of M (a great storyline itself).

Infinity Gauntlet is a favorite of many. Cosmic Marvel is pretty great too, here's the order. The Inhumans story starts at the end of Secret Invasion, so if you want to read that, you could jump into Cosmic Marvel toward the end of Cosmic Marvel or the beginning of War of Kings.

It really depends on how much you want to read and what sounds interesting. Are you looking for a specific character's storyline? A team? Or just something with universe-wide implications? What DC do you like?

Moon Knight's origin is probably among the most confusing in comic books. I have not read it. He has dissociative personality disorder and there's no consensus on whether or not he actually has super powers. It does not appear to be on Marvel Unlimited. To summarize it, Marc Spector is the son of an abusive rabbi who becomes a heavy weight boxer and marine (mercenary depending on the writer) who's such a jackass that his group of soldiers guns him down in an Egyptian tomb band gun him down and leave him for dead in front of a statue of Khonshu, the Egyptian god of the moon and protector of those who travel at night. Khonshu agrees to bring him back to life as his avatar. Upon returning to the United States, Spector's personality fractures into an investment manager Steven Grant, who makes him a millionaire off of his earnings as mercenary, and a taxicab driver, Jake Lockley. These two personalities allow him to mingle with elite arms dealers as well as street-level thugs and keep tabs on them all. The money he made as Grant also bankroll many of the gadgets he uses.

So I guess I'll be getting a Marvel Unlimited subscription.
